label: KD
reason_kind: change to the definition of correct
reasoning: The work item itself was to make the grader treat a previously-noted extra act as a failure — that is, to redefine what counts as a passing run, not to fix a defect in an existing definition. The rule on closing states that a shown result closes work and the human's own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery, 'never leaves a row open... unless [the definition of done] names his eye as the check' for one of three reserved cases: a taste call, a trade-off no artifact settles, or a change to the definition of correct. Here the verified, passing unit tests are an artifact, but they only confirm the code implements the redefinition mechanically — they cannot settle whether the redefinition is right, because the very thing that changed is what 'correct' means for a recorded run. The delivered state shows this is not a bug (the code does what the instruction said, nothing is broken) and not merely cosmetic: four recorded runs whose every material field is unchanged now read red solely because the passing criterion moved, dropping the score from 30 to 26. That is a direct, material consequence of redefining correctness, discovered only once the change was applied against real recorded runs — exactly the case the skill carves out for the person's word rather than the verifier's confirmation. Closing here on the verifier's say-so would treat a definitional shift with retroactive effect on prior evidence as an ordinary buildable result, which the skill explicitly distinguishes from the three reserved cases. So the checkpoint stays open, the four newly-red runs and the scoring shift are shown, and the Director asks whether this is the intended reach of the change before the work counts as closed.
